paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness plugin: remembers past conversations as a small graph
Context Graph for DeepSeek Harness
Memory for your chats, on from the moment you install it.
Later chats get a few lines that point at what was decided; the model fetches the exact text only wh
a few lines that point at what was decided; the model fetches the exact text only when it needs it.

**The problem.** Every message you send re-sends the whole conversation, and a new chat knows
nothin
g about the last one. You re-explain, the model re-reads, and you pay input tokens for both.

**What this does.** In every chat (memory is on by default), the plugin indexes what was
decided int

o a small graph of topics, each stored together with the original messages. Other
chats in the same
workspace get, at most, a few lines like this appended to your message:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The model calls `recall("c3n12")` when a gist is not precise enough and gets the original turns,
wor
d for word. Nothing is summarised away, and nothing is sent that you did not ask for.

> **First principle:** save input tokens without losing quality. A few lines per message; exact
> te

xt on demand.
>
> **Turning it off.** Plugins page → Context Graph → switch it off: no chat is index

ed or gets
> anything added. To stop only one chat, run `/context-graph off` in it.
## Quick start

1. **Plugins → Add plugin**, official npm registry, type `dsh-context-graph`, install, then fully
re

start the app (new slash commands need a restart).
2. Chat as usual. Every chat indexes itself every

4 turns and is shared with the other chats of
its workspace. Type `/context-graph`, pick it from th

e menu, then `build` to index one right away.
3. Open a new chat in the same workspace and ask about

something from the first.
4. To keep one chat out of the others, run `/context-graph unshare` in it

something from the first.
4. To keep one chat out of the others, run `/context-graph unshare` in it.
Command line instead of the Plugins page (the desktop app uses the `desktop` profile):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Commands

All commands are `/context-graph <word>`. Type `/context-graph`, pick it from the menu, then type
th

e word. Results show in dsh's own command card: a one-line summary that expands to the details.
No w

ow in dsh's own command card: a one-line summary that expands to the details.
No word means `stats`.
### `on` — resume memory for this chat
Memory is already on in every chat. `on` undoes an earlier `off` and indexes the chat right away.

Indexes the chat right away and then again every 4 human turns (one small auxiliary model call
each

time, using the chat's own routed model unless you configure another). Creates
`.context-graph/chats

/<chat>/` with the chat's graph, its verbatim sources and a `meta.json`
holding its title, dates and

flags. From now on every message you send in this chat is matched
against the other shared chats of

the workspace, and the first message of the chat also carries the
list of those chats, newest first

the workspace, and the first message of the chat also carries the
list of those chats, newest first.
Card: `Memory on · 7 topics in this chat · 2 shared chats to draw on`
### `off` — stop memory for this chat only
To stop it in every chat, switch the plugin off on the Plugins page instead.

Stops indexing and stops adding anything to your requests. The graph folder stays on disk, so
`on` l
ater resumes where it left off. Other chats keep seeing this chat if it is shared.
### `share` / `unshare` — keep a chat private, or share it again

Every chat is shared by default: other chats with memory on can match and recall its topics.
`unshar
e` makes this chat private; `share` undoes that. Nothing is copied or merged: the graph stays in its

own folder with its own dates, and its
ids carry the chat number (`c3n12`) so every hit traces back

to where it came from. Both take
effect at once. A chat shared
before its first index has nothing t
o offer yet; it fills in every 4 turns or with `build`.
Card: `Shared with the workspace · 7 topics`
### `stats` — where things stand (default)

First line: memory on/off, topics in this chat, shared/private, how many shared chats are
visible, h

ow many of this chat's turns are waiting to be indexed, and `update available` when a
newer version

is on npm. The body shows the version, the memory folder, and counters since the app
started: builds

and builder tokens, injected blocks and their size, recalls, and the main
conversation's input spli

t into uncached, cache-read and cache-write with the cache-hit rate. A
high cache-hit rate is the si
gn that memory is saving money rather than spending it.
Card: `Memory on · 7 topics in this chat · shared · 2 shared chats · 3 turns waiting to be indexed`
### `build` — index this chat now

Runs the indexing call immediately instead of waiting for the next 4-turn mark. Useful right
before

you switch chats. Needs memory on. If the model's answer cannot be read, the raw output is
saved to
`last-builder-output.txt` in the chat's folder and the card tells you why.
Card: `3 topics indexed (2 new) · this chat has 7 topics`
### `map` — every chat in the workspace

Lists all indexed chats newest first: chat id, start date, title, topic count and flags (`this
chat`

, `memory on`, `shared`/`private`), each followed by its most connected topics with their ids.
This
is the text form of the graph; a visual page is planned.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### `find <words>` — search the shared chats

The same matcher the plugin runs on your messages, so you can see what the model would be shown.
Tim

e words narrow it: `find 524 timeout last week` looks in chats active last week first. Only
shared c

hats of other conversations are searched; the current chat's own topics are left out
because they ar
e already in its context.
[该节后续省略]
## What it costs
| Moment | Added to the request |

| Chats without `on` | nothing |
| First message of a chat | about 15 tokens per shared chat, 20 cha

ts at most |
| Every later message | nothing when no topic matches; under about 150 tokens when some

do |
| Indexing | one auxiliary call every 4 turns, off the critical path; roughly the new text in,

under 1k tokens out |
| `recall` | one tool round trip with the exact text |

Injected blocks are appended to the end of your newest message, never inserted earlier, so the
provi

der's prefix cache keeps working. DeepSeek bills cached input at a small fraction of the
uncached pr
ice; protecting that cache matters more than shaving a few lines.
